channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United States: Labor stability tempers Fed hike risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ macro team led by Oscar Munoz expects headline US Nonfarm Payrolls to slow to 80k in June, with 55k private and 25k government jobs, marking a return to breakeven job growth. The Unemployment Rate is forecast to edge down to 4.2% as participation slips.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish bias sustained with one more hike – ING
item.description: ING’s Michiel Tukker and Benjamin Schroeder argue that reduced Oil sensitivity in rates and lingering uncertainty should prevent a strong dovish turn from the ECB.

item.title: Euro: Resistance at 1.1450 caps upside against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s FX strategists report that EUR/USD is softer as regional inflation data point to downside risks for national CPI, even as ECB President Lagarde signals that more tightening could come. Swaps price modest additional tightening by September.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Supported against Euro as NOK flows increase – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Senior Macro and FX Strategist Sara Midtgaard notes that the Norwegian Krone (NOK) weakened in June, with EUR/NOK peaking near 11.35, but now sees limited further upside.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains after Canada's GDP growth tops forecasts
item.description: USD/CAD trims its intraday gains on Tuesday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) strengthens after the latest Canadian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data surprised to the upside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4203 after hitting an intraday high of 1.4247.

item.title: WTI Oil advances amid improving Hormuz shipping, mixed risk outlook
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades higher on Tuesday, hovering around $70.80 per barrel at the time of writing, rebounding despite ongoing uncertainty surrounding relations between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Copper: China PMI support, US tariff risk – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht notes that the LMEX index remains under pressure even as China’s manufacturing PMI edges above 50, supporting Copper via AI-driven exports.

item.title: United States CB Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.2 in June
item.description: US consumer sentiment gains terrain in June, as the Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rises to 91.2 from May’s 90.6 (revised from 93.1).

item.title: Breaking: US JOLTS Job Openings increased to 7.594M in May
item.description: According to Tuesday’s Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), job openings totalled 7.594 million at the end of May.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Scope seen for recovery against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that recent improvements in Canadian growth data justify a more constructive view on the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that USD/JPY has broken above its 2024 highs near 162, reaching levels last seen in the 1980s, with traders focused on potential Bank of Japan (BoJ) action.

item.title: Gold steadies after sliding to fresh seven-month low, Fed rate-hike bets weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds on Tuesday after falling to a fresh seven-month low of $3,941 in the Asian session, as dip buyers help the precious metal recover some of its losses. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,024.

item.title: US Dollar: Modest upside scope as risks recalibrate – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong notes that the US Dollar (USD) softened slightly as global risk appetite improved on easing geopolitical tensions and a tech rebound.

item.title: Bank of England: No change expected in 2026 – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley outlines her baseline view on Bank of England (BoE) policy, citing softer United Kingdom (UK) Consumer Price Index (CPI), lower Oil prices and a slack labour market.

item.title: Economists Agree: 2026 Oil price forecasts lowered as Strait of Hormuz shipping improves – Reuters poll
item.description: According to a Reuters poll published on Tuesday, analysts have lowered their 2026 Oil price forecasts for the first time since the Iran war began as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz gradually improves, easing concerns over prolonged supply disruptions.

item.title: Euro stabilizes vs Yen amid softer German inflation, Japan intervention warnings
item.description: EUR/JPY trades modestly higher on Tuesday, hovering around 185.10 at the time of writing, up 0.07% on the day. The pair is supported by a resilient Euro (EUR) despite softer-than-expected German inflation data.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Range trade persists against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that USD/INR is trading in a tight range, with robust foreign portfolio inflows into Indian debt and supportive domestic factors offset by a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) stance.

item.title: British Pound trades sideways against the Japanese Yen as traders weigh intervention risks
item.description: GBP/JPY trades in a narrow range on Tuesday, struggling to build on the previous day's gains as traders remain wary of a possible intervention by Japanese authorities after the Japanese Yen (JPY) weakened to a fresh 40-year low against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: United States: Sticky inflation and Fed skepticism – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Taylor Schleich and Vy Le note that United States (US) growth expectations remain healthy, with GDP projected to expand above 2% in 2026, but they see a less benign inflation outlook.

item.title: British Pound: Neutral stance against US Dollar with carry support – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the Pound (GBP) remains resilient to local political developments and fiscal risks, supported by foreign inflows into gilts and the Bank of England’s (BoE) reluctance to ease policy amid resilient growth and disinflation.

item.title: Germany annual CPI inflation softens to 2.3% in June vs. 2.5% expected
item.description: Annual inflation in Germany, as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), softened to 2.3% in June's flash estimate from 2.6% in May. This print came in below the market expectation of 2.5%. On a monthly basis, the CPI declined 0.3% following the 0.2% decrease recorded in May.

item.title: Gold: Deep quarterly loss on Fed repricing – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch reports that Gold briefly dipped below USD 4,000 per troy ounce before bargain buying emerged, yet the metal is still heading for its largest quarterly drop in 13 years and a steep monthly decline.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens against US Dollar, eyes on US JOLTS Job Openings data
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) as the latter outperforms amid firm expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at least once this year.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD struggles around $4,000, near YTD lows
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades right above the $4,000 psychology¡gicval level at the time of writing, after hitting fresh year-to-date (YTD) lows at $3,941 earlier on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Momentum fading as data and Warsh loom – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that the Dollar has been giving back recent gains against G10 currencies as equities recover and risk sentiment improves. He highlights expectations for stronger US consumer confidence and softer JOLTS openings, which should still signal a healthy labour market.

item.title: Australian Dollar steadies as hawkish RBA minutes meet firm US Dollar ahead of labor data
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.6890 on Tuesday, holding steady on the day as investors digest the latest Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) monetary policy meeting Minutes while remaining cautious ahead of key US labor market data.

item.title: Euro: Fiscal strength and reserve status – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas strategists highlight that despite weaker post-Covid productivity than the United States (US), the European Union retains stronger public finances and growing international use of the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Euro underperforms amid doubts over further ECB rate hikes through year-end
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is down against its major currency peers, trading 0.17% lower to near 1.1400 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains supported against US Dollar due to lower Oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades subduedly against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro trims gains against British Pound despite positive German Retail Sales figures
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades lower against the British Pound (GBP) for the second consecutive day on Tuesday, with price action approaching 11-month lows at 0.8600.
